action: Minister Robert Troy advises credit union members to be extra vigilant over transactions and payment requests, and to contact their credit union with concerns; BleepingComputer adds vigilance for phishing and impersonation.
date_note: Reported Nov 18; the attack ran October 2 to 4, 2026.
exec: A shared IT supplier's incident potentially involves saved payee records at about 40 Irish credit unions; BleepingComputer says the supplier lacks activity logs to confirm which payees were affected.
plain: A Belfast software supplier used by Irish credit unions was hacked, exposing members' saved payee details such as names and bank account numbers.

key_findings: Wellington IT supplies about 50 credit unions, 43 in Ireland; about 40 affected, at least six have disclosed.
An automated script made five million requests exploiting an authorization flaw with valid credentials, October 2 to 4.
Saved payee records exposed; passwords, PINs and card details reportedly not.
recommendations: Watch for payment fraud and phishing.

summary: About 40 Irish credit unions are affected by a breach at Belfast supplier Wellington IT, which calls it a cyber security incident. BleepingComputer, citing the Irish Examiner, says an automated script exploited an authorization flaw around October 2 to 4; The Register says the flaw was closed on October 6. Saved payee records were exposed; passwords and PINs were unaffected, BleepingComputer says. The Irish Times says it could affect as many as 1.8 million people. Minister Robert Troy called the delay "not acceptable".
title: Around 40 Irish credit unions hit by Wellington IT supplier breach

validation.note: Compared BleepingComputer with RTE: about 40 credit unions, breach in October, credit unions told November 17, Troy called delay not acceptable, Wellington IT working with DPC, NCSC and Garda. RTE does not give the request count or dates; other outlets report differing figures (1.4 million vs five million requests, October 2-4 vs October 6), so those are attributed to BleepingComputer only. Follow-up 22 November: The Irish Times (17 November) says more than 40 credit unions (43 in its headline) and up to 1.8 million people potentially affected, its own estimate; it says Wellington IT was contacted and reports no reply. No later statement from Wellington IT found.

review.note: minister quote 'not acceptable'; action advice replaced with Troy/BleepingComputer advice; script claim attributed to BleepingComputer citing Irish Examiner; log claim attributed; evidence for about 40; published days

evidence.quote: Around 40 credit unions in Ireland were affected, roughly a quarter of the national total.
the potential breach could impact as many as 1.8 million people or over half of the credit union members in Ireland.
